Implementation plan — digital timeline

Three 90-day cycles aligned to school terms, preceded by inception/diagnostic work and followed by consolidation.

Plan-driven workflow
Phase 0

Inception & Mobilisation

Oct 2026

Confirm school list, reporting requirements, M&E framework, governance and pilot diagnostic instruments.

Phase 1

Diagnostic & Baseline

Oct 2026 – Jan 2027

Establish the documented 'before' picture for leadership, teaching, curriculum and learner performance.

Cycle 1

Stabilise

Jan – Mar 2027

Put core routines in place: HOD observations, ATP tracking and functioning PLCs.

Cycle 2

Deepen Teaching Practice

Apr – Jul 2027

Improve classroom practice, run observe-feedback-reobserve cycles and conduct the midline review.

Cycle 3

Accelerate Learner Performance

Jul – Sep 2027

Target learner results and transfer ownership of the improvement cycle to school leadership.

Close

Consolidation & Handover

Sep – Oct 2027

Endline, final evaluation, school handover packs, district summaries and close-out.

Analyse → Action → Create

The programme's repeated improvement loop becomes the system workflow.

01 · Analyse

Use learner results, curriculum coverage, lesson observations, school diagnostics and PLC data to identify the priority gap.

02 · Action

Assign focused support: adjusted plans, catch-up sequencing, specialist coaching, remediation, moderation or leadership action.

03 · Create

Leave sustainable tools and routines behind: trackers, PLC protocols, observation schedules and school-owned improvement practices.

Weekly / Monthly

Fortnightly

Ongoing

Evidence Submission

Within programme workflow

Differentiated school support

The diagnostic phase places each school into one of three support tiers, which sets contact frequency and focus.

01
Intensive

Tier 1 — Intensive

Weak leadership routines and low results across phases.

  • Weekly specialist contact
  • Leadership coaching every visit
  • High-frequency intervention monitoring
02
Targeted

Tier 2 — Targeted

Functional leadership with specific subject or phase gaps.

  • Fortnightly specialist visits
  • Priority subject / phase focus
  • Targeted follow-up actions
03
Light-touch

Tier 3 — Light-touch

Routines in place and results closer to target.

  • Monthly visits
  • PLC support
  • Data-use support

Support-frequency monitoring view

The monitoring environment can compare expected support frequency with recorded programme activity.

Contact due

Automatically identifies schools that require a specialist contact this week based on support tier.

Overdue intervention

Flags follow-up actions that have passed the agreed target date without closure evidence.

Support intensity analysis

Compares intervention volume with school tier to identify possible over- or under-support.

School analytics — from stakeholder evidence to action

The school dashboard keeps leadership, teachers, curriculum, learners and improvement actions connected to the same School ID.

School-first analysis
SMT
Principal / SMT / HOD

Leadership assessment and recurring leadership evidence.

  • HOD observations: planned + written feedback
  • PLC evidence: minutes + attendance + data item
  • Decision use: coaching & leadership priorities
TCH
Teachers & classroom practice

Teacher records are linked by teacher code rather than shown as an unsupported school total.

  • Needs analysis: phase / subject / development need
  • Observation: rubric + feedback + evidence
  • Response: coaching or training action
ATP
Curriculum

Weekly ATP monitoring is kept at grade and subject level.

  • Due vs completed: ATP units
  • Instructional time: planned vs delivered
  • Action: HOD sign-off + catch-up plan
LRN
Learner assessments

Results can be analysed by evaluation round, grade and subject.

  • Learners assessed: 100 sample per round
  • Result fields: score totals + mark bands
  • Evidence: authorised anonymised extract
ACT
School improvement action

Evidence is translated into a school response through the Analyse → Action → Create loop.

  • Need: finding or gap
  • Action: targeted support / catch-up / remediation
  • Review: next reporting cycle

POPIA-aware design

The implementation plan identifies learner data privacy as a programme risk. The digital system therefore separates operational access from analytical access, supports anonymised learner datasets where appropriate, and keeps restricted information behind approved access controls.

Quality assurance controls

Instruments are piloted before use, observation ratings are calibrated, attendance is captured promptly, and a sample of school data is checked against source records monthly.

System principles visible in the workflow

Single point of entry

The web application domain is the user's entry point into the full programme environment.

Role-based dashboards

Each stakeholder sees the monitoring information required for their responsibilities.

School-first analysis

Each school keeps its own measurement path, interventions, evidence and dashboard before results are aggregated.

One reporting source

Dashboards, downloadable reports and evidence outputs use the same structured programme records.
